sections.title: Introduction: Beyond 3D Space
sections.content: Briefly review the distance formula in 2D (Pythagoras) and 3D. Define an n-dimensional sphere as the set of all points at a distance 'r' from the origin in n-dimensional Euclidean space.
sections.example: Visual: Transition from a 2D circle to a 3D sphere, then a 'wireframe' morphing into a 4D hypersphere representation.

sections.title: Mathematical Framework: The General Equation
sections.content: Introduce the equation x₁² + x₂² + ... + xₙ² = r². Explain that as dimensions increase, we simply add more squared terms, representing degrees of freedom.
sections.example: A 2D coordinate grid vs. an n-dimensional coordinate list [x₁, x₂, ..., xₙ] representing a point.

sections.title: The Paradox of Concentration of Measure
sections.content: Explain that in high dimensions, almost all the volume of a sphere is concentrated near its surface (the 'crust').
sections.example: Animation: An orange representing a sphere where the 'peel' gets progressively thicker relative to the total volume as we move from 3D to 10D.

sections.title: The Empty Space Phenomenon
sections.content: Demonstrate that high-dimensional spheres are surprisingly 'empty' at the center and corners, a key concept in Machine Learning (the curse of dimensionality).
sections.example: A robot trying to navigate a hypersphere—it finds that 'nearby' points are actually very far apart in terms of data distance.

sections.title: Application: Why it matters
sections.content: Briefly explain how high-dimensional spheres are used in data clustering, cryptography, and neural network weights.
sections.example: A neural network organizing 'cat' vs 'dog' image data as points on the surface of a high-dimensional sphere to maximize distinction.

storyboard.title: Introduction: Beyond 3D Space
lecture_lines: Pythagoras works perfectly in two dimensions.
Extending to three, we simply add a Z-term.
Generalize this to n-dimensions using n coordinates.
The distance formula naturally scales to any dimension.
Thus, we define spheres in n-dimensional space.
animations: Animate appearance of a 3D cube in center (#3498DB).
Morph cube into a higher-dimensional hypercube wireframe (#E74C3C).

storyboard.title: Mathematical Framework: The General Equation
lecture_lines: The n-dimensional sphere follows a standard equation.
Sum the squares of all coordinates.
This total equals the radius squared.
animations: Display Equation: E = MC^2 at center (#FFFFFF).
Highlight variables M and C in gold (#F1C40F).
Animate transition of M into a variable vector V (#2ECC71).

storyboard.title: The Paradox of Concentration of Measure
lecture_lines: Volume concentrates near the surface in high dimensions.
Most of the sphere's mass lies near the crust.
This behavior is counter-intuitive for low-dimensional intuition.
Visualizing this, the crust dominates the volume.
Volume concentration is a fundamental geometric fact.
animations: Show a sphere representing a high-dimensional space (#FFFFFF).
Show mass concentrating near the equator of the sphere (#E67E22).
Fade in distribution curve showing concentration of points (#9B59B6).
Display text 'Most points lie near the equator' (#FFFFFF).
Pulse the concentrated area to emphasize the paradox (#E74C3C).

storyboard.title: The Empty Space Phenomenon
lecture_lines: Points seem distant despite being close.
This sparsity impacts machine learning performance.
animations: Visualize volume of high-dimensional sphere vs cube (#FFFFFF).
Shrink sphere volume while cube remains constant (#3498DB).
Fade in text showing 'V_sphere approaches zero' (#E74C3C).

storyboard.title: Application: Why it matters
lecture_lines: Data points live on high-dimensional manifolds.
Clustering algorithms rely on sphere geometry.
Neural networks leverage these high-dimensional spaces.
animations: Display a neural network graph structure (#FFFFFF).
Show data flowing through the network nodes (#F1C40F).
